exceptions.rationale: Reviewed the v0.45.0 Linux amd64 evidence-oid4vci local reproduction from review-only rehearsal 41317676125 on 2026-11-01. The pinned distroless cc-debian13 nonroot base, complete ordered DiffIDs, production OCI process contract, native Grype/Syft inventories and assertion file digests were checked against the exact exported rootfs. Grype reports wont-fix with no fixed version for libc6 2.41-12+deb13u4. Debian's trixie tracker still marks this CVE vulnerable and records <no-dsa> (Minor issue); Grype's wont-fix enum is a scanner representation, not a promise that Debian will never fix it. The carried libc/resolver implementation remains present. The reviewed application executables import and contain none of ns_printrrf, ns_printrr, ns_sprintrrf, ns_sprintrr or fp_nquery, and no reviewed dynamic lookup selects them. The bounded source paths do not enter the affected TSIG diagnostic-printing functions; ordinary resolver initialization does not establish that path. The reviewed reports exposure/evidence-oid4vci.json record no review-required dynamic lookup in /usr/local/bin/evidence-oid4vci; their resolved constant lookups select only __pthread_get_minstack, _dl_find_object, getrandom, none of which selects an affected symbol or library. The shipped load path selects the process-local OfferStore; the PostgreSQL and sealing backend is neither called by that entrypoint nor selectable in configuration. Candidate acceptance still requires the exact ordered rootfs layers, production OCI process contract and Syft-bound executable, loader, libc, libm and libpthread digests. The owner and invalidation triggers remain unchanged; the approved quarterly review expires on 2027-01-26.

Proposed risk acceptance for owner review: the v0.45.0 Linux amd64 evidence-oid4vci local reproduction from review-only rehearsal 41317676125 was reviewed on 2026-11-01. Native Grype reports CVE-2026-84243 as High and not-fixed with no fixed version for libc6 2.41-12+deb13u4; Debian also still lists this package as vulnerable without a fixed version. The affected gettext implementation remains in libc and can be reached internally by ordinary error reporting. Exploitation additionally requires non-C LC_MESSAGES, attacker-controlled LANGUAGE across an environment trust boundary, and a crafted readable .mo catalog. In the exact Debian glibc source, guess_category_value reads the current category and returns for C or C.<encoding> before consulting LANGUAGE; POSIX is stopped before catalog loading. Programs start in C, and libc does not call setlocale itself. Independently cross-checked GNU and LLVM ELF reports cover /usr/local/bin/evidence-oid4vci; their loaded closure is only the executable, loader, libc, libm and libpthread. Neither the applications nor their non-libc loaded libraries import global or thread locale setters, and source review found no compiled locale-changing path or such constructor. pg_query NLS is compiled out where present; AWS-LC constructors perform CPU and cryptographic initialization. The exact exports contain no locale catalogs, and the pinned nonroot OCI processes set only PATH and SSL_CERT_FILE. These reviewed processes retain their startup C locale; locale environment variables alone do not change it. The runtime and operator-tool reports, where present, have no review-required or unlocated dynamic lookup. All resolved application dlsym lookups select only __pthread_get_minstack, _dl_find_object and getrandom, not locale or gettext entrypoints. The exact ordered DiffIDs, production OCI process contract, native Grype/Syft inventories and assertion file digests were checked against the exported rootfs. The whole application-layer binding covers every shipped operator tool as well as the entrypoint. Locale/gettext calls, a changed runtime or tool dependency closure, deployment-supplied native libraries, or plugin/extension enablement require re-review under the existing exposure-assertion and runtime invalidation rules. This is a conditional exposure decision for the reviewed Linux amd64 processes, not a dependency fix. The proposed owner is @jeremi and expiry remains 2027-01-26.

Reviewed the v0.45.0 Linux amd64 evidence-oid4vci local reproduction from review-only rehearsal 41317676125 on 2026-11-01. The base carries zlib, including gzwrite, gzfwrite, gzprintf and gzvprintf. The reviewed application executables neither need libz nor contain libz.so, gz_vacate, gzwrite, gzfwrite, gzprintf or gzvprintf. No reviewed dynamic lookup opens that closure, and the bounded source paths expose no stalled gzip-write followed by formatted-output operation. The reviewed reports exposure/evidence-oid4vci.json record no review-required dynamic lookup in /usr/local/bin/evidence-oid4vci; their resolved constant lookups select only __pthread_get_minstack, _dl_find_object, getrandom, none of which selects an affected symbol or library. The shipped load path selects the process-local OfferStore; the PostgreSQL and sealing backend is neither called by that entrypoint nor selectable in configuration. The public Token Status List codec uses pure-Rust miniz_oxide, not system libz or its gz* routines, and no shipped entrypoint calls that module. Candidate acceptance still requires the exact ordered rootfs layers, production OCI process contract and Syft-bound executable, loader, libc, libm and libpthread digests. The owner and invalidation triggers remain unchanged; the approved quarterly review expires on 2027-01-26.

Reviewed the v0.45.0 Linux amd64 evidence-oid4vci local reproduction from review-only rehearsal 41317676125 on 2026-11-01. The pinned distroless cc-debian13 nonroot base, complete ordered DiffIDs, production OCI process contract, native Grype/Syft inventories and assertion file digests were checked against the exact exported rootfs. Grype reports wont-fix with no fixed version for gcc-14-base 14.2.0-19. Debian's trixie tracker still marks this CVE vulnerable and records <no-dsa> (Minor issue); Grype's wont-fix enum is a scanner representation, not a promise that Debian will never fix it. The carried libstdc++ aligned operator-new implementation calls posix_memalign with the unrounded requested size and imports neither aligned_alloc nor memalign. libgcc_s and libgomp define no aligned operator new; libgomp separately imports memalign for its OpenMP allocator. The reviewed application executables need none of libstdc++, libgcc_s or libgomp, import no C++ symbols and contain no aligned operator-new names. The complete representative base-ELF scan found no libstdc++ or libgomp consumer and only libstdc++ itself needing libgcc_s. Relevant base-library bytes match across all ten exports, and every application executable was checked separately. No reviewed application or dynamic lookup reaches that C++ allocation closure. The reviewed reports exposure/evidence-oid4vci.json record no review-required dynamic lookup in /usr/local/bin/evidence-oid4vci; their resolved constant lookups select only __pthread_get_minstack, _dl_find_object, getrandom, none of which selects an affected symbol or library. Candidate acceptance still requires the exact ordered rootfs layers, production OCI process contract and Syft-bound executable, loader, libc, libm and libpthread digests.
